title: Nyelvcsere
intro: You join a language exchange evening. Everyone chats in Hungarian. Get your verb endings right!

a.speaker: Tímea
a.textEn: Hi all! Are you learning Hungarian too?

b.speaker: Tímea
b.textEn: And why are you learning Hungarian?

choices.textEn: Because I think it's very interesting.

c.speaker: Tímea
c.text: Szuper! És otthon milyen nyelven beszéltek?
c.textEn: Great! And what language do you speak at home?

choices.text: Otthon angolul és néha egy kicsit magyarul beszélünk.
choices.textEn: At home we speak English and sometimes a little Hungarian.

choices.note: About your own household: mi → beszélünk.

choices.textEn: Sorry! At home we speak English.

d.speaker: Tímea
d.text: Te tudsz németül? A barátom osztrák, és ő nem tud magyarul.
d.textEn: Do you speak German? My boyfriend is Austrian, and he doesn't speak Hungarian.

e.speaker: Tímea
e.text: Én sem tudok jól németül. Otthon angolul beszélünk.
e.textEn: I don't speak German well either. At home we speak English.

choices.note: Her last sentence was positive (we speak English), so: Mi is!

end-great.text: Tímea laughs: “Akkor angolul is beszélhetünk!” (Then we can speak English too!)

end-ok.text: Almost! After a positive sentence it's is, after a negative it's sem.
